name: Isle Of You Naturally Farm Retreat
description: The Best Choice for your Clothing Optional Nudist Retreat. Where our friendly commitment to the nude lifestyle,  encourages people to be free.  Imagine your experience here starting the day naked on the deck. Enjoying coffee,fruits,yoga,and watching the world go by.
neighborhood_overview:
We are located on a rural one lane road going from sea level-1000ft. It's a nice quiet stroll up and down Kama'ili Rd. It starts off Highway 130 and ends at Opihikao on the red road, another amazing one lane road along our east coast with the cleanest air in the world.
There are no street lights in this area, so you are guided by the stars and moon light. With very little noise on the farm you'll rarely hear cars, neighbors, sirens, etc. You will hear leaves falling, chickens squawking during the day, and maybe your lovers heartbeat.
host_about:
a decade ago,  my husband bailed on the mainland and all its stress to buy a 70 acre farm on the Big Island near Pahoa. We are a working farm located on the east side of the island of Hawaii, about 30 min south of Hilo on the Puna Coast, close to the quaint village of Pahoa.
We spend our days tending to gardens, the fruit orchards, maybe a day at the local black sand beach called Kehena, playing volleyball or just watching sunsets.
Our guests tend to be outdoor types who love to be in nature.  We invite you up for coffee if you'd like or you can hang by yourself and we'll ignore you if that's what you want.  Then you'll be in your own little paradise and only contacting us when you need info or want to chat.
A couple of mottos to live by include:
'Ua mau ke ea o ka'aina i ka pono o Hawaii'  -- The life of the land in Hawaii is preserved in righteousness.
'Aloha mai no, aloha aku; o ka huhu ka mea e ola ' ole ai' ---When love is given, love should be returned; anger is the thing that gives no life.

description: Kona's best & most requested location.  It is only one of two resort condos at  a white sand beach in Kona. host_about:
KonaDave is a coffee farmer and world traveler!  His great, great, great uncle brought the first coffee plants to Kona in 1828, the rest is coffee history.  

He was born in Seattle, Washington and when not traveling the world splits his time between homes in Kona, Hawaii, and Edmonds, Washington. He travels over 100 days a year. He grew up (friends say he never grew up) in Seattle and graduated from the University of Washington before a career in the newspaper business and advertising. He worked for a Washington Post company and the San Francisco Chronicle. 

He "retired" from the newspaper business when his daughter was born in 1987. When she was three months old KonaDave started traveling the world.  His daughter left dirty diapers in 24 countries before she was three. KonaDave has explored over 100 nations and states around the world. Italy is his favorite to visit.   He also runs a real estate investment company between travels.  

He loves to show people Hawaii's hidden treasures and his KonaZona Coffee Farm, Art  Gardens and Tiki Village.  Come visit him at the farm and he will let you pick all the coffee, fruit or flowers to take back to the condo.  He will share and cup of Kona Coffee or Mai Tai in his backyard Tiki Bar.  If you are lucky one of his famous parties will happen when you are in town.  They are legendary!!  The KonaZona is only 4 miles and 100 years away in historic Artist filled Holualoa town.  KonaDave  and the famous KonaZona Coffee Farm, Art Garden and Tiki Village  are easy to find on the internet. Check it out on your internet explorations of the Big Island!

The diversity of this island paradise and the wonderful snorkeling and the lovely townhouse settings made all the other complexes pale in comparison on our searches - we purchased townhouse #59 and returned for our fifth trip to completely redo the unit (tile to ceiling) in preparation for personal and guest visits.  We still feel the same way about this wonderful place and now own a second, completely oceanfront unit (#196) in this same lovely complex.  And, it's only gotten better. Super clean, well maintained, simple and beautful decor, plenty of space to pack away our suitcases and settle in comfortably, good beds & linens, and complete kitchens for at home meals whenever we like. And, if there's ever a problem; resolving it is our top priority.  We don't want our guests to worry or be inconvenieced wherever possible.

Here’s a breakdown, month-by-month, of what’s going on (and where) in Maui.

January: Chinese New Year Celebration (Lahaina)
February: Chinese New Year Celebration (Lahaina), World Whale Day (Kihei), Maui Open Studios Art Events (all areas), Maui Plein Air Painting Invitational (Lahaina, Kapalua)
March: Whale & Ocean Arts Festival (Lahaina)
April: Banyan Tree Birthday Party (Lahaina), Maui County Agricultural Festival (Wailuku), Haiku Ho’olaule’a & Flower Festival (Haiku), Maui Steel Guitar Festival (Kaanapali)
May: East Maui Taro Festival (Hana), Maui Onion Festival (Lahaina), Maui Brewers Festival (Kahului), Maui Classical Music Festival (Makawao, Hana, Makena), Maui Matsuri (Kahului), Wa’a Kiakahi Sailing Race (Kaanapali)

name: The Maid's Quarters Cottage with Gardens and Gazebo Hot Tub
description: Open windows to let mountain breezes flow through a little house that's big on character. neighborhood_overview: The cottage is in the Hale Ohia Tract, a residential historic district of Volcano Village on a one lane road with no thru-traffic. The diversity of this island paradise and the wonderful snorkeling and the lovely townhouse settings made all the other complexes pale in comparison on our searches - we purchased townhouse #59 and returned for our fifth trip to completely redo the unit (tile to ceiling) in preparation for personal and guest visits.  We still feel the same way about this wonderful place and now own a second, completely oceanfront unit (#196) in this same lovely complex.  And, it's only gotten better.  Our goal in rentals is to offer what we'd want and expect in a unit if we were traveling.  Super clean, well maintained, simple and beautful decor, plenty of space to pack away our suitcases and settle in comfortably, good beds & linens, and complete kitchens for at home meals whenever we like.  Fortunately for us, many of our guests appreciate and expect the same type of accomodation and we have several guests or groups of guests that have become repeat visitors to our lovely place/s.  All have said this is the best place they've found and the first place they check for return visits.  We love and appreciate all of our guests but even more so our repeat or referred guests.  We'd be delighted to welcome you and your friends to a stay in paradise. Our motto in life - pay it forward; be the first to do the right thing; set the right example; good karma will follow you.  Our guests should know that we will do everything to help them enjoy their stay with us.  It's a point of pride for us - no cutting corners, etc...we want and expect that guests continue to say how nice they expected it to be and how much nicer it actually was.  And, if there's ever a problem; resolving it is our top priority.  We don't want our guests to worry or be inconvenieced wherever possible.

description: Welcome to historic old Hawaii. Charming old refurbished COTTAGE with 3 bedrooms -delightful walled garden compound. This vacation cottage is set in a garden with 3 other cottages. neighborhood_overview:
Hilo has a 'retro vibe' that is charming to many who come here. Hilo has a more than average number of artists & creatives.There is a fusion of cultures and cuisines which make for some interesting small restaurants around town and there are several places to eat and listen to live music.
Browsers might enjoy the thrift stores or vintage stores. The 'famous' Hilo Farmers Market is one block from this property.

Hilo is a great place for guests to enjoy slowing down & it is a great base for those with a long 'bucket list' of sights on the East side of the island:
lava viewing, stargazing, botanical garden, waterfalls, Waipio valley and more. Hilo is central to all of these sights.
host_about:
Aloha I'm Megan. Meet Jasper also. We've been working to create a colorful atmosphere for visitors that reflects the beauty of the tropics. Both of us enjoy helping guests feel comfortable so that they can relax and enjoy all the magic of this wet and wild side of the island. 

Hilo could become known as 'the town that time forgot' because it has the flavor of an older, slower Hawaii. In that way we are pretty easy going and relaxed ourselves. We have two guest cottages and a romantic 1 bedroom apartment here at The Lotus Garden. This is a property that features two garden courtyards, stone Buddha statues, a fish pond and an abundance of tropical plants and trees. . The Lotus Garden is reminiscent of the former 'sugar cane plantation days' when houses were clustered together so that there was a sense of community in the way people lived. Here Travelers meet other travelers in passing. Another wonderful feature of The Lotus Garden is that we are right in the center of town. Guests enjoy being a block away from the Farmer's Market and within walking distance of our cafes, restaurants, galleries and even Hilo's own Kava Bar. 

Just ask us. .. we know some great little beach parks close by and some special things to do around Hilo..  

... Our latest creed to live by? "Now is a really good time!" And so it is..

Kirpal Meditation and Ecological Center is a half mile from the ocean on the eastern tip of the Big Island of Hawaii, approximately seven miles from the small village of Pahoa. The 10-acre ocean-view property is blessed with average daytime temperatures of 85° F year-round, and 65° F at night, with cool, fragrant trade winds, surrounding tropical flora, including old growth mangoes, nearby swimming, surfing and snorkeling.

This property was once a papaya farm and is now newly planted with bamboo, papaya, palms, banana and many other fruit trees. The octagonal Balinese meditation pavilion is set among shade-trees with an expansive view of the ocean. The island wildlife is all around us – a variety of birds by day and at night there's the pleasant chirping of Coqui frogs – and there are no snakes. Natural wonders include Volcanoes National Park, for lava and crater viewing, volcanically heated warm ponds and steam vents (as outdoor saunas) and other wonders of the lush tropics.

Kmec opened in the summer of 2008 for pre-arranged seasonal meditation retreats and private meditation-vacations on request. Additionally, we would like to extend our welcome to Big Island travelers offering cozy cottages and open air kitchen and bath. We offer daily free meditation instructions and practices at our beautiful Balinese meditation pavillion. Additionally, we offer Yoga and nature tours upon guest's request (donations accepted).

host_about: I love to travel!  I've been very blessed to enjoy traveling as a child while my dad was in the military and then as an adult for my job and with my husband.  We began visiting Hawaii in 1999 and our annual visits turned into our first purchase of a vacation home in 2006.  It was on our 4th trip to the Big Island of Hawaii and during our 2nd stay at the Keauhou Kona Surf and Racquet Club that we began looking for our own place.  The diversity of this island paradise and the wonderful snorkeling and the lovely townhouse settings made all the other complexes pale in comparison on our searches - we purchased townhouse #59 and returned for our fifth trip to completely redo the unit (tile to ceiling) in preparation for personal and guest visits.  We still feel the same way about this wonderful place and now own a second, completely oceanfront unit (#196) in this same lovely complex.  And, it's only gotten better.  Our goal in rentals is to offer what we'd want and expect in a unit if we were traveling.  Super clean, well maintained, simple and beautful decor, plenty of space to pack away our suitcases and settle in comfortably, good beds & linens, and complete kitchens for at home meals whenever we like.  Fortunately for us, many of our guests appreciate and expect the same type of accomodation and we have several guests or groups of guests that have become repeat visitors to our lovely place/s.  All have said this is the best place they've found and the first place they check for return visits.  We love and appreciate all of our guests but even more so our repeat or referred guests. description: This rustic and cozy cabin sits on our 5 acre parcel in the cloud forest above Kona town on the Big Island, called Kaloko Mauka. host_about:
Kirpal Meditation and Ecological Center is a half mile from the ocean on the eastern tip of the Big Island of Hawaii, approximately seven miles from the small village of Pahoa. The 10-acre ocean-view property is blessed with average daytime temperatures of 85° F year-round, and 65° F at night, with cool, fragrant trade winds, surrounding tropical flora, including old growth mangoes, nearby swimming, surfing and snorkeling.

This property was once a papaya farm and is now newly planted with bamboo, papaya, palms, banana and many other fruit trees. The octagonal Balinese meditation pavilion is set among shade-trees with an expansive view of the ocean. The island wildlife is all around us – a variety of birds by day and at night there's the pleasant chirping of Coqui frogs – and there are no snakes. Natural wonders include Volcanoes National Park, for lava and crater viewing, volcanically heated warm ponds and steam vents (as outdoor saunas) and other wonders of the lush tropics.

Kmec opened in the summer of 2008 for pre-arranged seasonal meditation retreats and private meditation-vacations on request. Additionally, we would like to extend our welcome to Big Island travelers offering cozy cottages and open air kitchen and bath. We offer daily free meditation instructions and practices at our beautiful Balinese meditation pavillion. Additionally, we offer Yoga and nature tours upon guest's request (donations accepted).

neighborhood_overview: Wai'anae is a blue collar neighborhood on the leeward coast of Oahu. You can travel to Waikiki, or Honolulu and essentially feel like you never left the mainland. Swarms of tourists on the beach, and mass retail. description: A place where you meet genuine and authentic islanders hosts who will look after you like family and don't be surprised to be spontaneously invited to share family meals. A home away from home; a place of true hospitality and friendship given with no reservations or expectations.  Mahalo and Aloha !:)
neighborhood_overview: The relax atmosphere of Hilo and the aloha spirit is prevalent everywhere here.
host_about:
Aloha!
A little about myself; 
I moved to the Big Island in 1993 from Guam after serving a short stint in the USCG during the Golf War,  then worked as an acute care nurse at our local Hilo hospital for the last 22 years.  

Ive remained mesmerized by this island’s amazing natural beauty, diverse ecosystems, terrains, and love the laid back lifestyle it provides which easily translated into me transforming my house to one I can happily and proudly share with those seeking to explore and experience this amazing island in a relaxed home setting.  

I'm originally  from the Micronesian Island of Yap,  known for its pristine water, manta ray dives ( check out the world-famous  Yap Divers ) and  its colorful and spirited bamboo war dance performed by bare chested natives in lion clothes and grass skirts, something I grew up doing.   
I embrace  cultural diversity and truly enjoy meeting people from all walks of life and all regions in the world.  I take pride in my house and the service that I provide my guests. I value my precious 'free' time by sneaking in sporadic reading here and there  and enjoying the outdoors; camping, hiking, swimming, kayaking, paddle board, and gardening, but most of all, I love traveling and looking forward to seeing a lot more of this amazing world we live in and experience different cultures along the way.

I’m always striving for a balanced lifestyle; healthy living through heath conscious cooking utilizing locally grown, ( a lot are my own home grown) produce, keeping physically active, and inner peace and serenity.   

I look forward to meeting you and I'm excited to host another amazing adventurous soul seeking to experience the Big Island of Hawaii!

name: Maui is OPEN! Come and visit your Oceanfront condo
description:
Maui is OPEN for tourists, after the devastating wildfires! Your condo is far away from Lahaina, and the people of Maui need you to visit their Island, to assist them recover financially from the fires!

Enjoy the spectacular, treetop, panoramic, view of Maalaea Bay and Haleakala, from your private lanai. Watch turtles feeding along the shoreline and in the winter see humpback whales jumping in the Bay. Your condo is far away from Lahaina, yet close to everything fun to do in Eastern Maui!
neighborhood_overview: Your top floor, ocean front condo has a treetop, panoramic 'million dollar' view of Maalaea Bay and the 10,043' Haleakala dormant volcano.  Listen to the surf lap at the shore a few feet below your private lanai.  Watch whales play in season out in the bay. Your condo is far away from the Lahaina fires, on the other side of the mountain.  Eastern Maui has hundreds of things to see and do, without bothering the recovery efforts in Lahaina.
host_about: I asked Karen to marry me when we were on the summit of Haleakala (10,043'), which can be seen from our 4th floor, treetop lanai. We were married by a remote waterfall on Maui a year later. Maui is very special to us!  Ma'alaea (Mah-ah-lie-yah) is a secluded, little village off the beaten path to Lahaina. Not many people know the town even exists and that is why we like it. It is centrally located to just about everything fun to do on Maui, but when you return back to your "Little grass shack", you seem to be miles away from everything and can relax and take time to smell the plumerias!!!  Aloha, Joe & Karen

description: This 2BR/2Bath ground-floor Palm Villas unit is private and secluded, surrounded by 6 acres of lush landscaping. The Mauna Lani resort exudes understated elegance and truly lives up to its name:

description: BBWK 2014/0002. TA146617958401, We are located in a residential neighborhood on the north shore of Maui in an area of Pa’ia known locally as Spreckelsville or Sprecks. neighborhood_overview:
Located in Spreckelsville on Maui’s beautiful North Shore, Sprecks Plantation House is the perfect place to enjoy all that Maui has to offer. Our updated accommodations offer a charming, tropical ambiance and private lanais (Hawaiian for patio). Listen to the gentle rustle of palms in the trade winds while you relax after a long day of sun, surf and adventure.

Centrally located, Sprecks Plantation House is walking distance to beautiful, white sand beaches. The classic town of Paia, just a few minutes by car, is home to a wide range of great restaurants, surf shops and art galleries.

If you are a windsurfer, kitesurfer and/or surfer, you’re going to love it here. Sprecks Plantation House is located right between Kite Beach and Ho’okipa Beach, the ‘Windsurfing Capital of the World’.

Kirpal Meditation and Ecological Center is a half mile from the ocean on the eastern tip of the Big Island of Hawaii, approximately seven miles from the small village of Pahoa. The 10-acre ocean-view property is blessed with average daytime temperatures of 85° F year-round, and 65° F at night, with cool, fragrant trade winds, surrounding tropical flora, including old growth mangoes, nearby swimming, surfing and snorkeling.

This property was once a papaya farm and is now newly planted with bamboo, papaya, palms, banana and many other fruit trees. The octagonal Balinese meditation pavilion is set among shade-trees with an expansive view of the ocean. The island wildlife is all around us – a variety of birds by day and at night there's the pleasant chirping of Coqui frogs – and there are no snakes. Natural wonders include Volcanoes National Park, for lava and crater viewing, volcanically heated warm ponds and steam vents (as outdoor saunas) and other wonders of the lush tropics.

Kmec opened in the summer of 2008 for pre-arranged seasonal meditation retreats and private meditation-vacations on request. Additionally, we would like to extend our welcome to Big Island travelers offering cozy cottages and open air kitchen and bath. We offer daily free meditation instructions and practices at our beautiful Balinese meditation pavillion. Additionally, we offer Yoga and nature tours upon guest's request (donations accepted).

host_about:
Aloha!
A little about myself; 
I moved to the Big Island in 1993 from Guam after serving a short stint in the USCG during the Golf War,  then worked as an acute care nurse at our local Hilo hospital for the last 22 years.  

Ive remained mesmerized by this island’s amazing natural beauty, diverse ecosystems, terrains, and love the laid back lifestyle it provides which easily translated into me transforming my house to one I can happily and proudly share with those seeking to explore and experience this amazing island in a relaxed home setting.  

I'm originally  from the Micronesian Island of Yap,  known for its pristine water, manta ray dives ( check out the world-famous  Yap Divers ) and  its colorful and spirited bamboo war dance performed by bare chested natives in lion clothes and grass skirts, something I grew up doing.   
I embrace  cultural diversity and truly enjoy meeting people from all walks of life and all regions in the world.  I take pride in my house and the service that I provide my guests. I value my precious 'free' time by sneaking in sporadic reading here and there  and enjoying the outdoors; camping, hiking, swimming, kayaking, paddle board, and gardening, but most of all, I love traveling and looking forward to seeing a lot more of this amazing world we live in and experience different cultures along the way.

I’m always striving for a balanced lifestyle; healthy living through heath conscious cooking utilizing locally grown, ( a lot are my own home grown) produce, keeping physically active, and inner peace and serenity.   

I look forward to meeting you and I'm excited to host another amazing adventurous soul seeking to experience the Big Island of Hawaii!  

Welcome & E Komo Mai!

Diana

neighborhood_overview:
The home is located in a beautiful residential community. The backyard and pool area is very large and is secluded from the neighbors due to the carefully manicured landscaping.

There is a beautiful walking trail/road above our home which is used by walkers and bicyclists.
(left out of the driveway, right on Nani Kailua. The next right or left will put you on the road. Going left is a dead end, going right will take you through some ranch land and then high end homes and lots. It is about a mile.)

host_about:
My husband John and I first fell in love with the Big Island over 30 years ago when we were hired to teach summer school  for a few years at Hawaii Preparatory Academy. This time allowed us to get to know the island and the people and helped us form lasting relationships. We just could not stay away. It is a magical place and we have spent many summers here with our family.  

After years of house trading with families we eventually were able to buy a vacation home.  One of our favorite things is to share what we know about the Big Island with others.  We are happy to answer questions and make recommendations. 

The home is spacious and we hope welcoming to families as well as multiple couples traveling together. We have had three other couples share our home with us and there is plenty of space. It allows for those wonderful evenings enjoying each others company and there is privacy when you want it.

host_about:
My partner Terry and I had been visiting South Kona from our home in Southern California for 16 years.  We finally broke down and bought our property on The Big Island of Hawai'i early in 2013.  We have a 30-tree mango orchard on our one-acre lot which sits about 800' above Kealakekua Bay.   We also own a lot very close to the property, and we are considering expanding the orchard.

We fell in love with South Kona and the expansive views of the coast and the sea - as well as the myriad of activities the area offers - ocean sports of all kinds, hiking, biking, running, etc.

I am retired and live on the property pretty much full time. Terry continues to run his own business and travels around the world.  We have a dog named Kona (we didn't name her - she came to us with that moniker!) who loves to play with tug toys.  If you visit, you'll see what we mean.

We are avid hikers, and I can steer you to some great spots near our property and around the island.  I study Hawaiian and Hawaiian culture at our local Community College, and I am becoming well-versed in matters of Hawaiiana.  I was a social worker, a therapist, a professor, a theatre director, and an actor.

We enjoy meeting new people and swapping tales of travels.  We love sharing our island with others.  Life is Good.  Come visit!

description: Kihei Akahi, C211 - 1 bedroom, 1 bathroom condo located ground floor with the most quiet & private lanai facing beautiful grounds, naturally shaded by trees, like your own private yard. A short walk to one of Maui's most beautiful beach's, Kamaole II. A perfect getaway for couples. Maui is called the “valley isle” or the “honeymooner’s isle” due to its laid back feel and natural beauty. If you’ve never been to Hawaii and only visiting one island, Maui will give you the best overall experience.
neighborhood_overview: South Kihei, and more specifically the Kihei Akahi complex, is perfectly located. Everything (shopping/restaurants/tour operators, etc.) you may need on your vacation is within walking distance if you do not want the expense of renting a vehicle. However Costco, Walmart and Target are near the airport, approximately a 20 minute drive from the condo. The area is safe and friendly, I call it a sleepy little town as most people call it a day around 10:00pm to get up early and enjoy the mornings and sunny days.
host_about:
I purchased this condo in 2013 after many years of searching for the perfect place to retire, I found it on Maui, more specifically South Kihei. The plan was to invest in a great retirement location and hope to someday spend winter months being "snowbirds" and enjoy it during retirement years. 

My wife of 12 years at that time, Tracy was diagnosed with cancer in 2013 and passed away in 2014, she never did get to see the place we purchased. With her spirit along side me, I continued to pursue our dream. While she was battling cancer and after her passing, the condo underwent a complete renovation and I continue to add and update things on a regular basis. 

Over the next several years I continued to work in Edmonton in a manufacturing setting at Quality Control in the oil and gas sector. During the summer of 2020, I met an amazing woman Michelle, who currently co-hosts with me. We both retired together in 2023 and spent our first winter in the condo with the plan to do so every winter from here on in. 

I have met so many great folks and am privileged to be able to open my second home to awesome guests from all over the world. I enjoy working closely with my guests and am happy to assist in your vacation getaway plans. Your job is to come enjoy this beautiful property and island, please feel free to contact me at anytime if you have any questions.

Life is short, enjoy it on the beach....

Mahalo
Perry

We enjoy doing quick shopping at the ABC Store and a little health food grocery store nearby. Fred's and Moose McGillicuddy's is a short walk South across from Kamaole III Beach and their Taco Tuesday nights are fantastic! Moose's has one of the only bars that has a beautiful ocean view, so be sure to check it out...and their Happy Hour is awesome! Kihei is a special place and when you visit...be careful because you may decide that you don't want to leave!!

description: Welcome! TheTropical Guest House has a clean lodge feel and is *easy to settle into. neighborhood_overview: The lava has cooled down, come check it out. Check out the Saturday morning farmers market in Kaimu.  Historical Pahoa town is just fifteen minutes away. host_about:
Aloha, I made a lifestyle decision to move to Hawaii in 2005. I fell in love with the Big Island for the first time in 97. Since then I've explored homesteading and a closer connection to our land. I have been building and creating. Now I am ready to share the house with travelers who visit this magical place. I am into a peaceful sustainable existence, that gives rest to a fast moving civilization. Sometimes it is enough to just look at the stars, and here you can see them well, or just return to the original TV, a nice relaxing fire. And I love to cook on the flames, so simple, so good. Sharing food is my favorite form of communion. I love slow cooking, whether it be smoking or stew making. Slower and longer is just better if you ask me. 

I am a builder, and as a builder the most gratifying thing is to see people enjoying the manifestations that have been created. Sometimes the focus of what it means to construct something for the utilitarian purpose gets lost in the process. But, the magic is always underlying everything, so many times pure serendipity is right there, reminding us. The intention is everything and construed in all the stones carried, wood carved, land sculpted and much, much else. When the energy is pure, then it is easily conveyed or felt. This land is unfolding as the volcano has taught us. All who become part of this history will see how powerful is the asking. My experience here is that there is an instant reflection in the asking. Have fun and come and see...After all this is some of the newest land on this planet.

description: Welcome to Hale Honu, "Home of the Sea Turtles"!   This 2 bed/3 bath private and gated OCEANFRONT HOME has additional space and can easily sleep 8 adults.  We designed Hale Honu to provide our guests with an experience in which everyone can slow down and become immersed in the presence of the ocean, filled with its rhythms and energy, and mesmerized by the waves and tropical fish below.   This is a sublime place to let the cares of the world drift away with the tide.  You'll love it here!
neighborhood_overview:
Laid back Ali'i Dr. is a 5 mile long meandering oceanfront drive with old Kona charm. Our beach house is about 3 miles south of old Kailua-Kona town. The park next door frequently plays host to local family BBQs, ukulele get-togethers and kid's hula classes. Live like kama'aina (locals) when you stay at Hale Honu.
Alii Drive is the main artery that runs along the ocean south of town. We find that the sounds of the ocean mask virtually all of the road noise. We'll hear a motorcycle or the garbage truck go by, but for the most part are unaware that there is a road bordering Hale Honu. The only windows in the house that face Alii Drive are in the hallway upstairs. 90% of the windows face the ocean.
host_about:
My husband, Peter, and I live in the Sierra foothills in California.  We have been vacation rental hosts for over 20 years- in Kona, Hawaii, Lake Tahoe and in Grass Valley, CA.  We also now own a little house on the Greek island of Skopelos which we will be adding to our list of rentals soon! 
We love our little pieces of paradise and enjoy sharing them with others.  We travel to our places in Kona and Skopelos as often as our schedules (and our 2 pugs!) will allow, always fine tuning things so our guests have the best experience possible. 
Our favourite place to spend the summer is Greece, but our favorite place to snorkel is right in front of our house in Hawaii (Hale Honu).  
Life at home is pretty sweet too.  We have a huge garden and recently started beekeeping.   
We love to travel, garden, and spend time in the kitchen- I mostly cook, he mostly cleans- so yes, we have a marriage made in heaven.

host_about:
Aloha!
A little about myself; 
I moved to the Big Island in 1993 from Guam after serving a short stint in the USCG during the Golf War,  then worked as an acute care nurse at our local Hilo hospital for the last 22 years.  

Ive remained mesmerized by this island’s amazing natural beauty, diverse ecosystems, terrains, and love the laid back lifestyle it provides which easily translated into me transforming my house to one I can happily and proudly share with those seeking to explore and experience this amazing island in a relaxed home setting.  

I'm originally  from the Micronesian Island of Yap,  known for its pristine water, manta ray dives ( check out the world-famous  Yap Divers ) and  its colorful and spirited bamboo war dance performed by bare chested natives in lion clothes and grass skirts, something I grew up doing.   
I embrace  cultural diversity and truly enjoy meeting people from all walks of life and all regions in the world.  I take pride in my house and the service that I provide my guests. I value my precious 'free' time by sneaking in sporadic reading here and there  and enjoying the outdoors; camping, hiking, swimming, kayaking, paddle board, and gardening, but most of all, I love traveling and looking forward to seeing a lot more of this amazing world we live in and experience different cultures along the way.

I’m always striving for a balanced lifestyle; healthy living through heath conscious cooking utilizing locally grown, ( a lot are my own home grown) produce, keeping physically active, and inner peace and serenity.   

I look forward to meeting you and I'm excited to host another amazing adventurous soul seeking to experience the Big Island of Hawaii!  

Welcome & E Komo Mai!

Diana

neighborhood_overview:
From Kamehameha the Great to Elvis Presley, discover the rich history of Waikiki from swampy farmlands to royal playground and how it became one of the most famous destinations in the world.

In early Hawaii, Waikiki was a much larger area than the 1.5 square miles it encompasses today. Old Waikiki, much of it swampland, included the neighboring valleys of Manoa and Palolo. Translated, Waikiki means "spouting water," a reference to the rivers and springs that richly flowed into the area.

In the mid to late 1800s, Waikiki served as a vacation retreat for the kingdom’s royalty. Kamehameha IV, Kamehameha V, Lunalilo, Kalakaua, Liliuokalani and Princess Kaiulani were among the dignitaries who maintained residences in the area, enjoying moonlight horseback rides, thrilling canoe races and carefree romps in the ocean.

name: The Onion House, Hawaii
description:
A wildly original architectural gem set on a high terrace overlooking the Kona Coast, the Onion House was built for the McCormick Spice family, by renowned architect Kendrick Kellogg. With the whole home to yourselves, you’ll relish the privacy to swim, sunbathe and enjoy the 70' pool in a lush tropical setting. Walls of screen and stained glass let you live in touch with the environment, so this experience is like luxury camping.

All guests must be 12+ years old.
neighborhood_overview:
With tropical rainforests, beaches, plunging waterfalls, snowcapped mountains, and an erupting volcano, the Big Island of Hawaii is a mini-continent containing nearly every climate on earth. Yet the Kona Coast, at 500’ elevation, sheltered by Mount Hualalai, is perhaps the only place with the gentle weather ideal for this very open style of building.
While in Kona, you can swim with manta rays or wild dolphins, fly over the erupting volcano, zipline through the treetops, sail, paddleboard, scuba, snorkel, or bodysurf. Minutes from the art village and galleries of Holualoa, and the Donkey Mill Art Center, the Onion House is the perfect base camp for your exploration of the rich diversity of the island.
A walking trail just above the house winds through an established older neighborhood with large trees. A very good French Restaurant is just a short walk down the hill. A number of excellent restaurants are within a five to ten minute drive.

host_about:
For 48 


years I've loved living in awesome North Kohala, fell in love with my special property when I first saw it in 1974, raised 3 children "roughing it" but loving adventures in a rural community, adopted 6 and fostered 7, taught school as a sub, K-12, painted landscapes in oil around the island before the family expanded to 9+ diverse kids, now want to resume my passion for creativity, hosted many musicians and folks interested in sustainable living, healthy choices, loving each other, God and country, and appreciation for our uniquely wonderful treasures here at the end of the rainbow.
I've really enjoyed meeting guests from all over the world and have made some lifetime friendships. Come visit! My daughter reminds me to "always keep smiling"…it's catching!

description:

Let your Hawaiian vacation begin.
Maui Vista is walking distance to all of your immediate needs and the Kihei weather can't be beat. Simply walk across the street and you will find Charlie Young Beach which is known for being one of the best & longest beaches in Kihei.

neighborhood_overview:
Nothing can beat this location! Walk to everything! If you want to get away from the high-priced Kaanapali area and get more of a local feel you have to try Kihei. The weather is known to be better than Kaanapali and there is plenty of shopping, snorkeling, sigh-seeing, golfing, water sports to go around! This area is laid back and affordable...not pretentious or high priced like other popular areas of Maui. Come check it out!!
Maui Vista is in the heart of Kihei. Wailea is a 5 minute drive. Lahaina a 30-45 minute drive depending on weekend traffic, walk outside your Lanai to the pool. Being a ground floor unit there is no need to carry groceries, luggage or kids very far. We are just steps away from parking and the main walking street along the beach. All that you need is steps away...
host_about:
I am a firefighter that LOVES to travel/vacation. After traveling the world I found Maui to be a little slice of heaven that I kept returning to again and again. With retirement on the horizon, I decided it was time to purchase a piece of paradise which I are happy to be sharing with all of you!
As a budget traveler, I have tried to provide you with all the comfort and requirements to make your vacation one to remember without busting the bank. I truly hope you love this place as much as I do. Mahalo

neighborhood_overview:
Two small towns are within 10 minutes in each direction. Naalehu has several restaurants (one of our favorites is Hana Hou) and the famous Punaluu Bakery (a must stop!), a hardware store, Shaka's bar (southernmost bar in the USA), post office and twice-weekly farmer's market. Pahala has a small grocery store - the Superette and a Long's drugstore. There's a hospital in Pahala and both locations have gas stations and a few other local businesses to explore.

The big agricultural attractions in the area are coffee and macadamia nuts; you'll see the farm lands all around. There are some local farms who offer tours and several coffee growers who offer tastings and direct from grower sales.

South Point (Ka Lae) and the Green Sand Beach (it really is green!) are located within about a half hour drive. Every visitor to Hawaii Island will want to see the world's most active volcano - Kilauea - in Volcano National Park. The condo is located 30 minutes from the park entranc
host_about:
We are Christen and Tom Mizikar, owners of Beechwood Cottage in the historic Ligonier Valley of Pennsylvania and Beachwood Punaluu in beautiful Hawaii.

We have been providing vacation rental stays since  before "Airbnb" was a verb! In our many years of hosting vacation guests, we've learned how to help you connect, relax, enjoy and experience two different, unique and special places.

Our cottage has an authenticity, style and setting that makes it special - from the 18th century chairs at the table to the giant stone fireplace to painstakingly hand-painted floors and hand-made draperies...we welcome you to respite under the shade of tall oak, hemlock, ash and poplar trees. 

Our condo is in just as unique location along the last undeveloped coast in all of Hawaii. We love to share the star filled skies, black sand beach and tall palm trees blowing in the tradewinds. Sit on the lanai and listen for the sound of the waves crashing into black lava outcroppings...look as far as one may see and fill your eyes with nature's beauty at Punalu'u, Ninole Cove or all along the Ka'u coast.

When we travel, we have high expectations for both destination and accommodation. We wouldn't have you stay in anything less than perfect for us - and we hope you'll find either (or both!) to be just what you are looking for in a short term lodging experience.

host_about: My family and I have been visiting the islands for the past decade. The first time we visited, we instantly fell in love with the people, culture, natural beauty, and of course, the food (and coffee) of Hawaii. After traveling to nearly all the islands (except for Niihau & Kahoolawe), we've always wanted to retain a connection back to our favorite state. After a few more visits, we decided that we wanted to get away from the busyness of Oahu, resort-like feel of Maui, and more isolated nature of Lanai/Molokai. The Big Island quickly emerged as our favorite island with its natural beauty, capacity to be explored, and people. Kona offers everything we've been looking for. Its beaches offer superb water sports and snorkeling, peace and quiet from the masses, and incredible diversity (black/green/white sand). The food is incredible (poke! Kona coffee!), locals laid-back and friendly, and the land offers nearly all of the climates our earth has to offer. Everything you could possibly want in an island, the Big Island offers. And we're so happy to officially call it our (second) home.

Location is everything when you are vacationing on Maui. We are located only 2 blocks away from Charley Young Beach, a beautiful white sand beach that offers swimming, sunning, strolling and snorkeling. Only 2 blocks in the opposite direction is the Cove Beach Park, which is an excellent spot for surfing, kayaking, paddle boarding, etc. Conveniently, rentals and lessons are available across the street from this beach. The unit is also a short 5 min walk from Kalama park, one of the largest beach parks on Maui, where you can find volleyball, basketball & tennis courts, a playground for the kids, roller skating rink, skate park and a boardwalk that runs parallel to the ocean.

host_about: Living in Upcountry Maui, we enjoy the cool breezes and beautiful view of the mountain and sea. We also enjoy the beautiful pool and BBQ area in the complex that makes for a fun afternoon after hanging out at the beach all day. description: Secluded studio with full kitchen, vaulted wood ceilings with exposed beams, ceiling fan, cozy lighting, wrap-around large lanai, coordinated color theme, garden views, paved roads, centrally located for visiting Volcanoes Nat'l Park, Mauna Kea, Hilo, Pahoa, and Kalapana. neighborhood_overview:
The best restaurants are in Hilo. My favorites are Cafe Pesto, Hilo Bay Cafe, and Reuben's Mexican restaurant. Cronies is another good one for great burgers and sandwiches. Kaleo's in Pahoa is a favorite of locals and visitors.

If you want to cook in and save money instead, I generally grocery shop at Target in Hilo because they have the most items at Mainland prices, but limited selection. Safeway is right next to Target and will have everything you need if you aren't too worried about prices. Foodland in Keaau is the closest to us (8 miles away) and I have a store discount card on your key ring for them. If you prefer health food stores, Kea'au Natural Foods is in the same shopping center as Foodland, right next to Ace Hardware. Island Naturals is in Pahoa and in Hilo.

Hilo also has some good beach parks for snorkeling and taking small kids to, but not much sandy beach areas. The Kona side has all the big, white sand beaches. My favorite beach is Punalu
host_about:
Joel and I realized our dream of moving to Hawaii in 2015 and we have an adult son who lives with us.  

Joel is a tech geek and can help you with any issues you may have.

We tend to keep to ourselves and not hover, but my goal is to make sure you have the most pleasurable stay as possible, so I'm counting on you to let me know if anything needs attention and I appreciate the opportunity to take care of it on the spot.

host_about:
Aloha!
A little about myself; 
I moved to the Big Island in 1993 from Guam after serving a short stint in the USCG during the Golf War,  then worked as an acute care nurse at our local Hilo hospital for the last 22 years.  

Ive remained mesmerized by this island’s amazing natural beauty, diverse ecosystems, terrains, and love the laid back lifestyle it provides which easily translated into me transforming my house to one I can happily and proudly share with those seeking to explore and experience this amazing island in a relaxed home setting.  

I'm originally  from the Micronesian Island of Yap,  known for its pristine water, manta ray dives ( check out the world-famous  Yap Divers ) and  its colorful and spirited bamboo war dance performed by bare chested natives in lion clothes and grass skirts, something I grew up doing.   
I embrace  cultural diversity and truly enjoy meeting people from all walks of life and all regions in the world.  I take pride in my house and the service that I provide my guests. I value my precious 'free' time by sneaking in sporadic reading here and there  and enjoying the outdoors; camping, hiking, swimming, kayaking, paddle board, and gardening, but most of all, I love traveling and looking forward to seeing a lot more of this amazing world we live in and experience different cultures along the way.

I’m always striving for a balanced lifestyle; healthy living through heath conscious cooking utilizing locally grown, ( a lot are my own home grown) produce, keeping physically active, and inner peace and serenity.   

I look forward to meeting you and I'm excited to host another amazing adventurous soul seeking to experience the Big Island of Hawaii!  

Welcome & E Komo Mai!

Diana

host_about:
Hi, we are an international couple, we're well traveled with us both living internationally for many years. We now live and enjoy a small corner of heaven know as the North Shore of Oahu, the birth place of surfing, yet still wild and full of beautiful beaches.    We're Honest, clean, tidy out going people and have an active,  fun lifestyle enjoying the amazing water sports here. I am renting out the spare studio attached to my house, to hopefully meet interesting people, share a bit of the "HI" life/aloha spirit and help pay the bills. 

We moved to Hawaii 7 years ago, thinking it would be a nice place to live for a couple of years, make some money and then get back to travelling. I under estimated how nice and how much fun it is to live here, and now I have a house here and no desire to leave. The laid back country atmosphere we have here on the North Shore is alluring- so much nicer than the crazy Waikiki tourist sausage machine.

I'm active and try to complete the whole range of sports possible here on the north shore. In fact my favorite days are when you get a "trifecta" - any three of the surfing, kiting, free diving SUPPing, mountain biking, motocross, beaching, hiking etc actives possible here.

One concept i live by is "Life is for the living"  I enjoy sharing these good times with other adventurous people. 

I work 9-6pm weekdays and other time am out surfing, kiting, adventuring etc. Im very tolerant  and respectful and because the house is still under repair everything is pretty easy going and relaxed.

Not a party house, but small gatherings are welcomed.

host_about:
KonaDave is a coffee farmer and world traveler!  His great, great, great uncle brought the first coffee plants to Kona in 1828, the rest is coffee history.  

He was born in Seattle, Washington and when not traveling the world splits his time between homes in Kona, Hawaii, and Edmonds, Washington. He travels over 100 days a year. He grew up (friends say he never grew up) in Seattle and graduated from the University of Washington before a career in the newspaper business and advertising. He worked for a Washington Post company and the San Francisco Chronicle. 

He "retired" from the newspaper business when his daughter was born in 1987. When she was three months old KonaDave started traveling the world.  His daughter left dirty diapers in 24 countries before she was three. KonaDave has explored over 100 nations and states around the world. Italy is his favorite to visit.   He also runs a real estate investment company between travels.  

He loves to show people Hawaii's hidden treasures and his KonaZona Coffee Farm, Art  Gardens and Tiki Village.  Come visit him at the farm and he will let you pick all the coffee, fruit or flowers to take back to the condo.  He will share and cup of Kona Coffee or Mai Tai in his backyard Tiki Bar.  If you are lucky one of his famous parties will happen when you are in town.  They are legendary!!  The KonaZona is only 4 miles and 100 years away in historic Artist filled Holualoa town.  KonaDave  and the famous KonaZona Coffee Farm, Art Garden and Tiki Village  are easy to find on the internet. Check it out on your internet explorations of the Big Island!

neighborhood_overview:
Waikīkī is a beachfront neighborhood of Honolulu, on the south shore of the island of Oʻahu, in Hawaii, United States. Waikīkī is best known for Waikīkī Beach, "a tourism mecca to both east and west creating a vibrant energy mixed with Hawaiian spirit."
The name Waikīkī means spouting fresh water in the Hawaiian language, for springs and streams that fed wetlands that once separated Waikīkī from the interior.
The area was a retreat for Hawaiian royalty in the 1800s who enjoyed surfing there on early forms of longboards.
A few small hotels opened in the 1880s.
Today, the area is filled with large resort hotels, such as the Hilton Hawaiian Village and the Sheraton Waikiki, and historic hotels dating back to the early 20th century (such as the Moana Surfrider Hotel and the Royal Hawaiian Hotel).
The beach hosts many events a year, including surf competitions, outdoor performances, hula dancing and outrigger canoe races.

name: Off grid Eco cabin Big Island Hawai
description: Affordable lodging on the East side of the Big Island in Hawaii. 35 miles from the Hilo Airport. This cabin has a screened in sleeping area upstairs with a Queen bed. Downstairs is an open air kitchen with a four burner gas cook top( no oven) and an outdoor shower,  flush toilet and sink.
neighborhood_overview: This area of Hawaii seems to appeal more to people who want to get off the beaten path and experience  Hawaii in a more natural, non-commercial way.Please note that this area of Hawaii does not have mega resorts, nightly  Polynesian shows, boogie board rentals, crowded beaches, or hoardes of tourists. It is a lovely area with hidden lanes, beautiful coastline, crashing waves, wild mango trees, pristine air, swimming  turtles, whales,dolphins, warm people, and recent flowing lava.
host_about:
Tom and I moved to Hawaii 5 years ago after we retired. We have a 5 acre property and with family are slowly creating a small farm, growing a variety of citrus, avocados,pineapple, bananas as well as  a variety of tropical fruits. We also raise chickens. All the dwellings on the property are totally off grid using solar energy and rainwater harvesting.Our vision is to create an off grid homestead and farm using organic growing methods and decreasing our carbon footprint. Our goal is to curb our personal impact on climate change and global warming, even if it is only in a very small way. As environmental activist, Bill McKibben,says "The problem with climate change is that it's very large, and as individuals we seem quite small against it, so it's easy for people to feel disempowered." We hope that in some small way, people who stay in our cabin, will feel empowered to make their own small changes. This can be as basic as a shift in thinking from mindless energy use to "mindful" energy usage, like turning out unneeded lights. We believe that millions of small changes can create big results
There is something magical about the sun providing your energy, the rain your water, and feeding the trees with your organic wastes.. We enjoy living simply and in harmony with the earth.We love interacting with people and enjoy the diversity it brings to our lives.

name: Tropical Bamboo Guest Cottage near Pahoa
description: Welcome to the Cottage! It is an all natural, hand crafted getaway in the jungle of the magical East side of Hawaii. The Cottage is one mile to Kehena beach, six miles to the new Po'hoiki black sand beach/hot pools, the new lava flows and many tide pools along the red road. The cottage is built with organic materials that were locally harvested, a true labor of love. It is a cozy nook to relax in under the umbrella of Pele's homeland.
neighborhood_overview: Ten minute walk to the black sand beach of Kehena, where there may be dolphins to play with. A short drive will land you at Unlce Roberts Kava bar, where you will often find the Uncles playing old Hawaiian country songs on Wednesday night. Also, at Uncle Roberts is the Saturday morning farmers market.
host_about:
Aloha, I made a lifestyle decision to move to Hawaii in 2005. I fell in love with the Big Island for the first time in 97. Since then I've explored homesteading and a closer connection to our land. I have been building and creating. Now I am ready to share the house with travelers who visit this magical place. I am into a peaceful sustainable existence, that gives rest to a fast moving civilization. Sometimes it is enough to just look at the stars, and here you can see them well, or just return to the original TV, a nice relaxing fire. And I love to cook on the flames, so simple, so good. Sharing food is my favorite form of communion. I love slow cooking, whether it be smoking or stew making. Slower and longer is just better if you ask me. 

I am a builder, and as a builder the most gratifying thing is to see people enjoying the manifestations that have been created. Sometimes the focus of what it means to construct something for the utilitarian purpose gets lost in the process. But, the magic is always underlying everything, so many times pure serendipity is right there, reminding us. The intention is everything and construed in all the stones carried, wood carved, land sculpted and much, much else. When the energy is pure, then it is easily conveyed or felt. This land is unfolding as the volcano has taught us. All who become part of this history will see how powerful is the asking. My experience here is that there is an instant reflection in the asking. Have fun and come and see...After all this is some of the newest land on this planet.

neighborhood_overview: Maalaea is probably no longer considered to be one of Hawaii’s “Best Kept Secrets”. The popular destination spots in Makena, Wailea, Kaanapali and Kapalua are all within a half hour drive of this small ocean front community. To explore the wondrous playground that is Maui, let’s start at the top and work our way down. Maui’s Haleakala Crater stands two miles above sea level. Hiking trails reveal a landscape of charred rock, cinder stacks and ash—more a moonscape than a place you’d associate with Earth. From there, head down the slopes into rain forests that ooze with Garden of Eden visions—400-foot waterfalls, tropical streams bordered with native trees such as ’ohi’a, ’olapa and kolea, and warm turquoise pools that invite an invigorating swim. Next, glide along the surface of the ocean on a surfboard or catamaran then dip below to greet a whole new world. Here, brilliant colors are the norm. It’s like diving into your own private "National Geographic" episode.

Day done—dig your toes into the sand, listen to the music of the waves and let your cares float away.

name: Relaxing Ocean View; Cathedral Ceilings!
description: Location, location, location! Centrally located in Sunny Kihei this meticulously maintained condo in the sought after Luana Kai Resort offers Vaulted Ceilings in every room, Porcelain Tile Floors, Granite Counter tops, Stainless Steel Appliances, &  an en-suite master bath. neighborhood_overview: Stay on the Sunny Side of the Island, minutes from many beautiful area beaches. 15 minutes from the Airport, and ten minutes away from the stunning golf courses of Wailea! Pickle Ball & Tennis Courts; Pool and Hot Tub on the grounds. Kihei is the most central location in Maui, close to all tourist points with great beaches for snorkeling and surfing nearby. Walk 400 feet to a beautiful walking beach right from the property grounds. No road between resort and beach. The beach has seasonal tides which sometimes bring coral with it, so we recommend the swimming beaches within half a mile in either direction. name: Explosive Volcanoes and Tropical Rain Forests
description: E komo mai to your home away from home. Relax on the open-air lanai with a cool cocktail or glass of wine. Prepare your meals in a gourmet kitchen. And you're only 5 minutes away from a clothing-optional, black sand beach. Enjoy whale watching in December - March.
neighborhood_overview:
Kalapana Seaview Estates (and this part of Hawaii) is made up of a diverse population - retirees, working class residents, many gay and lesbian yuppies, hippies, various nationalities and religions. The area is known as Puna, Kehena, or even Kaimu.

Don't be shocked if you see a dog riding on top of a car or on a motorcycle (with owner, of course).

Chat with your neighbors if the occasion arises. Invite a passer-by up to the lanai for a glass of wine! We are a friendly community, and we all have different experiences to share and advice to provide. We call it "talk story".
host_about:
Kevin and I have traveled around the world as tourists and travel writers.  David grew up in Maine. Kevin is from Long Island, NY. We've spent lots of time in Maine,  Paris and Apt (France), New Zealand, Budapest, La Penita (Mexico), New York City, Hartford, and Dallas.  And now the Big Island of Hawaii.

Motto: Being a success and never stopping to enjoy it is like buying a bottle of fine Champagne and never popping the cork. 

We are quiet travelers, however enjoy soft adventure: sky diving, zip lines, cruises on freighters, working in national parks. Fine foods and wines make us smile, and we enjoy food carts from Australia to Morocco. Our kitchen is a busy place!!

Live shows on Broadway or in theaters around the world are always at the top of our to-do list.

The joy we have experienced during our own travels has inspired us to open our cottage to guests from the globe's many cultures. We love to share our experiences and knowledge, and we look forward to hosting you. A hui hou!

name: Kihei Garden Estates - Steps from the Beach!
description: Great location to explore the island, relax by the pool, read or nap on your private balcony. Imagine the morning sun, the lush garden view, the tropical birds, the glorious beach & sunsets just steps away. These moments and so many more evoke the feeling and spirit of Aloha. Beach, restaurants, shops, groceries are a short 2 min walk away. The complex is small, in a low density area. Our much loved Kihei condo is upstairs, on a corner, with an exterior private entrance making it feel like home.
neighborhood_overview:
Our condo is located in a neighborhood and the bedroom windows face the street. You may hear some noises from the street at times (usually never an issue). If you are a light sleeper, there are fans and an A/C in the master and guest bedroom that provide white noise. The local street and neighborhood add to the charm of the condo and the complex.
The part we can’t say enough about is the feeling in Kihei: the trade winds, sunsets, waking in the morning to the local birds cooing, the Hawaiian “laid back” style of living in Kihei Garden Estates all add to its charm. The complex has been carefully planned to take full advantage of paradise island living. You have to experience it first hand to fully appreciate it. Let our condo be your Maui Ohana (home). Discover true aloha spirit. Experience the magic of Kihei.
host_about:
Aloha Friends!   

Our Maui home has been in our family for over 40 years and is very dear to our hearts.  My husband and I purchased it from my mother in 1999 and we have spent many wonderful moments there with our three, now grown children.   

We love to travel and have visited many places around the world, however,  our favorite place on earth is Maui , our happy place. 

Nothing brings us more pleasure than to share our little piece of paradise with others.   We hope you will soon be a part of our Ohana (extended family).  

With Aloha,

Leigh Ann and Dennis

name: Kohala Loke Lani, Big Island
description:
Please find us by doing a search for Kohala Loke Lani

An expansive ocean and mountain view cottage with a salt water pool located near prime Big Island beaches. This is a large studio ohana that comfortably sleeps two. There are big ocean and mountain views. In the winter months you may even see whales from the lanai!

You can follow our adventures on Insta gram at PamelaWonderWoman

You can find us by searching for Kohala Loke Lani
neighborhood_overview:
The ohana is located on the Kohala Coast of the Big Island. This is a lovely quiet place to visit. All of the houses here sit on lots of a minimum of 1.3 acres.

This region is considered to be desert. We average only 10 inches of rain per year. During our "rainy" season (August-November) our brown grass turns green. Most of the time, it is a dry, desert climate.
host_about:
Outgoing, fun loving, adventurous, friendly, animal loving artist who loves living in Hawaii.  I really enjoy having the opportunity to share the paradise of the Big Island with others.  The Big Island is alive and vibrant like very few places on earth.  It is a spectacular place to live.  

Before coming to Hawaii I used to travel the globe - Europe, the USA, SE Asia, New Zealand and Australia, but find that I don't like to leave my island quite as often anymore.  I was an avid budget traveler who never found a youth hostel or tent I didn't like.  Hawaii is a great jumping off point to Asia, so I see Japan in my future.  I recently made it to Korea!

As a host I'll see you to say hello and welcome you to the ohana.  If you need anything I'm in the next building.  I want your stay to be a pleasant one and your experience on the island to be filled with aloha.

description:
Altho the fires of Lahiana are devastating, Maui businesses need your support. Please visit! The rest of the island is open & just as beautiful as always!!

Let your Hawaiian vacation begin.
Maui Vista is walking distance to all of your immediate needs and the Kihei weather can't be beat. Simply walk across the street and you will find Charlie Young Beach which is known for being one of the best & longest beaches in Kihei.

**Ask us about renting the condo right next door - perfect for families
neighborhood_overview:
Nothing can beat this location! Walk to everything! If you want to get away from the high-priced Kaanapali area and get more of a local feel you have to try Kihei. The weather is known to be better than Kaanapali and there is plenty of shopping, snorkeling, sigh-seeing, golfing, water sports to go around! This area is laid back and affordable...not pretentious or high priced like other popular areas of Maui. Come check it out!!
Maui Vista is in the heart of Kihei. Wailea is a 5 minute drive. Lahaina a 30-45 minute drive depending on weekend traffic, walk outside your Lanai to the pool. Being a ground floor unit there is no need to carry groceries, luggage or kids very far. We are just steps away from parking and the main walking street along the beach. All that you need is steps away...
host_about:

name: King Room
description: Master suite upstairs in private home with super comfortable king cal memory foam bed comes has its own private bathroom with tub and hand held shower head.   Bamboo flooring, koa wood trimmings, porch with expansive view, far ocean view and gorgeous sunrises.  Bonus room set up with refrigerator, coffee machine and electric kettle.
neighborhood_overview: Nice, upscale cool (climate), and fairly quite.  We do have the infamous coqui frogs but they are not as abundant in this certain area.  I do provide earplugs should it turns out to be an annoyance.  Most of my guests actually enjoy the 'soothing' sound at night.
host_about:
Aloha!
A little about myself; 
I moved to the Big Island in 1993 from Guam after serving a short stint in the USCG during the Golf War,  then worked as an acute care nurse at our local Hilo hospital for the last 22 years.  

Ive remained mesmerized by this island’s amazing natural beauty, diverse ecosystems, terrains, and love the laid back lifestyle it provides which easily translated into me transforming my house to one I can happily and proudly share with those seeking to explore and experience this amazing island in a relaxed home setting.  

I'm originally  from the Micronesian Island of Yap,  known for its pristine water, manta ray dives ( check out the world-famous  Yap Divers ) and  its colorful and spirited bamboo war dance performed by bare chested natives in lion clothes and grass skirts, something I grew up doing.   
I embrace  cultural diversity and truly enjoy meeting people from all walks of life and all regions in the world.  I take pride in my house and the service that I provide my guests. I value my precious 'free' time by sneaking in sporadic reading here and there  and enjoying the outdoors; camping, hiking, swimming, kayaking, paddle board, and gardening, but most of all, I love traveling and looking forward to seeing a lot more of this amazing world we live in and experience different cultures along the way.

I’m always striving for a balanced lifestyle; healthy living through heath conscious cooking utilizing locally grown, ( a lot are my own home grown) produce, keeping physically active, and inner peace and serenity.   

I look forward to meeting you and I'm excited to host another amazing adventurous soul seeking to experience the Big Island of Hawaii!  

Welcome & E Komo Mai!

Diana

name: Steps to beach!!
description:
**Please note that due to Honolulu County ordinance, rentals must be 30 days or more.

Enjoy a part of real Hawai'i in our newly remodeled 1 bd/1 bath unit, across the street from the beach in a truly local community. Wile away the hours on the secluded beach or in the hammock under the mango tree. Surf, fish or relax and rejuvenate!
neighborhood_overview:
Your retreat home is in a local, working beach community, far from the hustle and bustle of Honolulu and Waikiki. On a stroll down the nearly empty beach you will find local fishermen, surfers, seashells, 'ama crabs, the occasional endangered Hawaiian monk seal and local families playing in the sand and surf.

As a historic neighborhood, Ewa Beach has become a blending of local, generational families and newer families who have seen the value in the sunrise to sunset views over the water. This is apparent as you drive down our little road - expansive multi-million dollar homes side by side with older plantation homes, residents leaning over the fence talking about their day. We see this as part of the charm of living in our community - the people here are quick to smile and give a friendly "aloha". This is not a touristy area, but more for the person seeking local charm.

Conveniences are not far away - for immediate needs, we have a little historic market, rig
host_about:
Aloha!! We are from Hawaii, although my husband is originally from Alaska and I spent many years in Washington State. We absolutely love to explore other cultures- it's our passion!  We love both the outdoors and the city.  We are pretty active with surfing, sailing, skiing, hiking and adventure travel, but we also love our down time spent reading, watching movies, walking the beach and relaxing. neighborhood_overview:
Puako Beach is an old beach front community dating back hundreds of years. Only within the past twenty years has the road been paved and it has become a desired location with multimillion dollar ocean front homes replacing many of the older local beach shacks. There are still some charming old-style places but the number is slowly dwindling as the real estate has become more valuable. It is the only neighborhood on the west side of the Island with easy ocean access without security gates and restricted access.
Some of our favorite times here are walking the dogs late at night on the deserted moon lit road, quiet early morning walks along the fire break open land behind our place, and early morning or evening ocean plunges at the County Park. (the swimming hole. See pic.)
Nearby eats in Kawaihae (15mn): Most days from 1pm to 5pm, down at the Blue Dragon parking lot, you can visit the most delicious Hawaii Shave Ice wagon on the planet!- pure snow with hundreds

We truly love meeting guests from all over the world and being able to share our unique and beautiful corner of the world, here in Hawaii.  Our experience with Airbnb guest has been exceptional and the response gratifying.

neighborhood_overview:
There are coral reefs directly in front of the resort if you enjoy snorkeling, and one of the oldest luaus on Maui is within walking distance (just past the park to the south).

Every day except Monday and Wednesday at 11:00 am, guests can try SNUBA in the pool for free. SNUBA is like SCUBA, except that you don't wear the tank, it floats on the surface in a raft and you have a long hose attached to your regulator. SNUBA does not require certification but allows you to get closer to the sea life than snorkeling. The instructor is also great with kids.

There's a nightly torch lighting at sunset and on some nights free live music by the Pailolo pool bar and fire-pit.

There are plenty of paid activities available from the on-site concierge including but not limited to: Outrigger paddle from the resort, Snorkeling excursions, whale watching (in season), Spa/Massage (on property), Luaus, etc.

host_about:
KonaDave is a coffee farmer and world traveler!  His great, great, great uncle brought the first coffee plants to Kona in 1828, the rest is coffee history.  

He was born in Seattle, Washington and when not traveling the world splits his time between homes in Kona, Hawaii, and Edmonds, Washington. He travels over 100 days a year. He grew up (friends say he never grew up) in Seattle and graduated from the University of Washington before a career in the newspaper business and advertising. He worked for a Washington Post company and the San Francisco Chronicle. 

He "retired" from the newspaper business when his daughter was born in 1987. When she was three months old KonaDave started traveling the world.  His daughter left dirty diapers in 24 countries before she was three. KonaDave has explored over 100 nations and states around the world. Italy is his favorite to visit.   He also runs a real estate investment company between travels.  

He loves to show people Hawaii's hidden treasures and his KonaZona Coffee Farm, Art  Gardens and Tiki Village.  Come visit him at the farm and he will let you pick all the coffee, fruit or flowers to take back to the condo.  He will share and cup of Kona Coffee or Mai Tai in his backyard Tiki Bar.  If you are lucky one of his famous parties will happen when you are in town.  They are legendary!!  The KonaZona is only 4 miles and 100 years away in historic Artist filled Holualoa town.  KonaDave  and the famous KonaZona Coffee Farm, Art Garden and Tiki Village  are easy to find on the internet. Check it out on your internet explorations of the Big Island!

Kauai is so lush and green it’s known as The Garden Island.

And what a garden! Waterfalls plunge into pools lined with exotic flowers, rare birds call out their unique songs, and waves peel off in long sonorous lines that whisper and fade on unspoiled beaches.

It is a garden tailor-made for exploration. Check out the Wailua River where, during certain times of the year and specific tides, you can view ancient stone carvings. Or, hike the Na Pali Coast—a 14-mile stretch of uninhabited shoreline where 2,700-foot cliffs plummet to clear coral waters, and hidden valleys open on empty white-sand beaches.

neighborhood_overview: Our home is located on a quiet cul-de-sac in an exclusive neighborhood in Holualoa. host_about:
Aloha!  We are a Kamaʻaina family providing an unique homestay for travelers.  We have been hosting guests in our family home since 2016. We are both from the islands; I was raised on Oahu and my husband Evan grew up in Waimea. Evan works as a freelance cinematographer. We stay busy with our two children-running from soccer and baseball practice to gymnastics class. We enjoy an active lifestyle of surfing, skateboarding, hiking and exploring the outdoors. On weekends, you'll often find us at the beach. We also love traveling and are excited to show our kids the world! 

We are fortunate to live on a beautiful one acre property in Holualoa. We are surrounded by mature monkey pod and palm trees and are at the ideal elevation above Kailua Kona. The forest behind our home is so peaceful and sunsets are amazing from our property! Nature surrounds us- everyday I see a variety of colorful birds. This home has also quite an interesting history as it is a custom home built for an Italian contessa who lived here for more than 20 years! 

Hawaii is a special and unique place. We enjoy sharing our place and why we love this island paradise we call home.

name: Step Into Serenity
description: Step Into Serenity...bask in the Spirit of Aloha. Tucked away from the hustle-and-bustle of Honolulu/Waikiki, but so convenient to many of the best beaches, activities, eateries, and shops, this peaceful retreat (you have use of the entire private home) is set on one acre of oceanfront property (not a swimming beach) facing Mokoli'i Island (Chinaman's Hat) on the windward side of O'ahu.  Tropical palate and vibe, as well as modern amenities, await you.  Amazing sunrises!  E komo mai....welcome!
neighborhood_overview:
Tucked away from everything....but a close commute to everything! Whether it's swimming, snorkeling, beach combing, horseback riding, ATV riding, hiking, exploring every nook and cranny of the island, taking in unparalleled beauty, sampling from O'ahu's diverse and delicious cuisine, you are in a convenient location from which to launch the day's activities. Just one mile up the road, the picturesque 153-acre Kualoa Regional Beach Park offers sweeping mountain and ocean views, picnic lawns, and beach access, while Kualoa Ranch & Zipline, a 4,000-acre private nature reserve and working cattle ranch, offers a plethora of activities: horseback riding, ATV riding, zip-lining, and tours of Hollywood film locations.
For a literal and delicious taste of Aloha, you'll want to visit
Tropical Farms Macadamia Nut Farm, just up the road from the vacation home, which began years ago as a simple roadside store and is now a quaint farm with a shop selling macadamia nuts, coffees, cho
host_about:
Born and raised in western Massachusetts, about as far away as one can possibly be from Hawai'i and still be in the United States, I arrived on O'ahu for a one-month vacation in 1980…but Hawai'i is hard to get out of one's system and I stayed to make Hawai'i my new home state. I’ve been exploring and loving the islands, people, and culture of Hawai'i for nearly four decades. I bought my first property on O'ahu in 1983, and during the 45-day escrow period, I earned my State of Hawai'i real estate license. Just two years later, I purchased the company I’d been working for; upon selling that business in 1986, I began and built my company, Fidelity Properties, from the ground up.  I purchased this beautiful (undeveloped) property in 1989 and built my home and the rental home and, over the years, I've nurtured the 'aina (land).  I enjoy swimming,  boating, and staying active.  Most importantly,  I am happy to share this paradise with you. 

Why this property?  "Keep the COUNTRY country."  You will see intermittent signs along the road on your way to the home.  The village of Waikane is in "the country"  away from the developed and more congested and populated areas of the island, and residents would like to keep it that way!  Here, there are flower farms and  and fruit trees.....a little bit of yesteryear and a country road that hugs the shoreline and takes you along an incredibly scenic drive along the windward coastline and onto the North Shore.  The quiet, windward side of O'ahu, from Kahuku to Kaneohe, is renowned for its lush vegetation, breezy trade winds, spectacular beaches, friendly little towns, and laid-back lifestyle.  With just about everything close at hand and several convenient avenues to Honolulu as well as the North Shore, it is no wonder I fell in love with and chose windward O'ahu, backdropped by the dramatic Ko'olau Mountain range, for my home and business base.  The nearest town is Kane'ohe, only a 15-minute drive, where you will find a variety of restaurants and shopping, a newly-expanded mall, movie theaters, and grocery stores.  

An acre of oceanfront, prettily landscaped with palm trees, flowers, and a lily pond, offers tranquility at the water's edge (the 'ae kai).....Sit and relax:  your view is the Chinaman's Hat sitting in the calm bay and the Ko'olau's rising steeply.  Forget your cares, feel anxiety slip away, savor the serenity.....

neighborhood_overview:
This Condo is just a five minute walk north to the huge Ala Moana shopping mall and close to the Honolulu Convention Center. Head south three minutes and you are at the newly re-constructed 'Duke Kahanamoku' public Lagoon on Waikiki beach, just in front of the Hilton Hawaiian Village Lagoon. The Lagoon has a sand bottom and the salt water is replenished five-times per day from the ocean using an elaborate pumping system. It is totally stocked with local tropical fish for your snorkeling pleasure (no sharks here!). Enjoy sunbathing on the sandy beach that totally surrounds the lagoon. Now that's what relaxing in paradise is all about.
If you prefer the ocean over the sand, there is access to one of the best surf spots on the south shore of Oahu, Kaisers and Bowls, close by.
